dataset.datasetnotes: Premilinary age control for the BL00-1E core was provided by C14 dates correlated from cores BL96-1, 2, and 3 with the upper portion of core BL00-1E, one magnetic excursion, and by a U/Th date at 66.4m on a fine-grained aragonite layer. Because the intial set of dates was restricted to the upper half half of the BL00-1E core, additional ages were inferred by direct correlation of the carbonate and isotopic data to the independently dated paleoclimate record from Devils Hole, NV. The age assessments suggest that the core extends back to about 225 ka, though should be interpreted with caution. Age model as presented here was provided by the authors.

site.sitedescription: Bear Lake is a large, deep lake located directly on the Idaho-Utah border in the northern Great Basin and is one of the few large lakes that survived Holocene desiccation in western North America. Surrounding vegetation: Many areas directly surrounding Bear Lake today have been converted to agricultural and developed land. Natural vegetation to the east, south, and north is largely Artemisia steppe and shrubland with Pinus edulis/Juniperus woodland on scarps to the east. To the west, with increasing elevations, are Populus tremuloides/Picea engelmannii/Abies lasiocarpa forest and woodland
